name: shiftwork_status
title: Shift work: status
description: Shift-work status: where ONE checkpoint file stands — units counted by status, the unit plan.cursor points at, how many handoff.open_questions are waiting, and the last history entry. Call it first when resuming a job or answering 'where is job X'; it is the cheap read before any clock-in. It does not say WHICH units may run now — that is shiftwork_plan, the dependency batches — and it says nothing about the server itself, which is bantamkit_status. Every fact is read from the checkpoint on this call, nothing is cached, and a checkpoint that is missing, not valid JSON or failing the checkpoint schema answers {"result": "error", "reason": "<sentence>"} instead of a partial summary — the same refusals shiftwork_plan and shiftwork_clock_in give for that file. With `search`, it also returns the lines of jobs Retention archived under the checkpoint's .shiftwork/archive/ that hold every word of the query. Opens only the checkpoint (and that archive directory when `search` is given); writes nothing, not even the log shiftwork_clock_in appends to.

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
checkpoint.description: Path to the shift-work checkpoint JSON file (by convention .shiftwork/checkpoint.json in the repo the job works on), absolute or relative to the server's working directory. The same file shiftwork_plan, shiftwork_clock_in and shiftwork_clock_out take; it must validate against assets/schemas/shiftwork-checkpoint.json.

search.description: Also search jobs Retention archived under this checkpoint's .shiftwork/archive/: every line holding all the query's words, as {job, file, line}.

result.description: `status` on success; `error` when the checkpoint could not be read or failed the schema, with `reason`.

cursor.description: The unit id plan.cursor points at.

units.description: Unit count per status, keys among todo, in_progress, done, blocked, dropped; a status no unit holds is absent.

open_questions.description: How many handoff.open_questions are waiting; non-zero means the next clock-in escalates.

last_history.description: The newest entry of the 5-entry history ring ({unit, outcome, notes?, ...}), or null when the ring is empty.

job.description: The archived job the line belongs to.

file.description: Path of the archived file, relative to the job.

search.description: Only when `search` was given: every archived line holding all its words, as {job, file, line}.

reason.description: With result `error`: one sentence saying why the call was refused.
